blocking_findings.scenario: The Record AC says record accepts each measured envelope using fixtures from the real runs, and the review context treats missing real-run evidence for any of the three runtimes as blocking. At this head, tests/IntentSystem.Cli.Tests/Fixtures/G834/ holds only codex-verdict.json and claude-envelope.json, and the real-run fixture test at lines 554-556 iterates only codex and claude. The HEAD commit (aeb2fce3) changed the cursor parser (CrossRuntimeReviewVerdict.TryParseTrailingObject, src/IntentSystem.Cli/Commands/CrossRuntimeReviewVerdict.cs:180) to strip progress narration that it describes as measured. The only cursor test (line 571) still uses a hand-built envelope `new { type, subtype, is_error, result = <bare verdict JSON>, session_id }`. It has no narration prefix, no real key set, and no real `result` text. No test exercises the narration-stripping path, and nothing in the repo shows the output of the pinned `cursor-agent -p --mode ask ...` invocation. Suppose a real cursor run wraps the verdict in a ```json fence, adds trailing text, or uses envelope keys that differ from the assumed `type`/`subtype`/`is_error` shape. Then every cursor verdict is refused as `cross-runtime-review-verdict-invalid`, and a declared team that uses cursor as conductor or cross-runtime reviewer can never satisfy the gate. Fix: add a trimmed cursor envelope fixture from the real run against this unit's PR head, and route it through `record` the way the codex and claude fixtures are.

notes: Checked: `git rev-parse HEAD` prints aeb2fce30cdae1f78fcfc8a8e2e8bc710d701412. Reviewed 9e461d8f..HEAD, the three commits after G833. The contract names `main` as the base; this clone has no local main, and 9e461d8f is the G833 merge the contract names as child main.

`gh pr view 90834 -R J-Tech-Japan/intent-system` fails with 'Could not resolve to a PullRequest'. So I could not check the PR body for the pasted real-run evidence, the base-vs-head pr-transition diff, full-suite counts, exact-head CI, or the required statement of the allow-list changes.

Focused Release tests (G834, AutomationPrTransition, GuideSoloConductor, Ledger filters) ran in a scratch copy of the head: 161 passed, 0 failed. I did not run the full suite. `git diff --check 9e461d8f HEAD` is clean.

No launch: the new CrossRuntimeReview*.cs files and ReviewCrossRuntimeCommand.cs start no process (the only match for 'Process' is a doc comment on the seam). The only new external read is `gh pr view --json headRefOid`, reached only for `approved` of a declared team in a gated repo.

Undeclared and ungated paths look unchanged by inspection. The gate is guarded by `transition == approved && IsGatedRepo(repo)`, an undeclared team returns (null, null), the new result field is WhenWritingNull, and the text line prints only when that field is non-null. Refusals return before the label write and before CI-wait clearing, in both write and dry-run.

The gate logic matches contract item 5. Other heads never count. Per runtime, the latest record on H decides. A blocked runtime clears only through its own later record. rereview-missing uses that runtime's latest record on an earlier head. Unreadable records force `blocked`. Relation is recomputed from the declared conductor runtime.
Records are written create-new (an existence pre-check plus FileMode.CreateNew for both the raw copy and the record), and the reader checks raw_verdict_sha256 against the copy.

Allow-list changes against the contract text: claude adds `--disallowedTools Edit,Write,NotebookEdit`, and cursor uses `--mode ask` instead of `--mode plan`. The contract allows run-driven changes if the PR states them with run output. The commit message explains the reason (a cursor plan-mode run wrote files), but I could not confirm the PR states it. Neither form contains a flag from the deny list.

The claude pinned form relies on plan mode plus removing the file-writing tools. Its own ReadOnlyEnforcement text says shell-level writes are not sandbox-enforced. That text is honest, but only codex is truly sandboxed. Consider whether that meets 'the reviewer must run read-only'.

Cursor `--mode ask` refuses shell commands, so a cursor reviewer cannot run `git rev-parse` or list the commits. The head it echoes then comes only from the prompt, which weakens the 'echoed head' binding for cursor. Worth stating in the guide.
The emitted verdict schema has no `$schema` draft 2020-12 keyword (the comment says Claude Code 2.1.269 rejects it). The contract says draft 2020-12, so the PR should state this deviation.

Minor: CrossRuntimeReviewStore.Read catches a fixed list of exception types, and pr-transition does not catch exceptions from Resolve, Read, or the claim reader. An unexpected exception crashes the command before any label write, so it still fails closed, but it does not report `record-unreadable` or `team-unresolved`.
